text.p: Malaysia's Land & General Bhd said on Wednesday that it expects a difficult year.
"The group expects the operating environment not to improve significantly for the year 1997," the property concern said in a statement releasing its results for the year ended December 31, 1996.
On Wednesday, it reported a 60 percent rise in 1996 net profit to 182.44 million ringgit, but just a three percent gain in turnover to 837.14 million ringgit.

On a pretax basis, it earned 242 million ringgit, up 26 percent from a year ago. But it noted that the year's results were helped by exceptional items related to the sale of its interest in stockbroker Rashid Hussain Bhd and writedowns of furniture and oil exploration asset values.
"Ignoring these exceptional items, the overall performance of the group's operations has been a severe disappointment," the statement said.
The disposal of shares brought it a 188.19 million ringgit gain and it also recorded a gain of 23.20 million ringgit from selling down shares in subsidiary companies.
Its core property business suffered setbacks, while its timber operations in Papua New Guinea and Australia experienced "awkward production and market environments", it said.
Land & General said it closed down two furniture factories.
